subject: Private Offer: NewtonCloud — request for nonstandard commission split & fallback policy
messages:
From: Ola Sundberg <ola@newtoncloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: NewtonCloud Sales Ops <salesops@newtoncloud.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer for NewtonCloud — request for commission change and fallback

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NewtonCloud is excited about moving forward with a private marketplace listing on AWS for our new managed discovery product. Before we finalize, procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a one-off adjustment to the marketplace commission split (they're requesting Redwood take 60% of net, rather than the standard 70/30 arrangement) and add a fallback if the private listing fails certification — so their customers can still purchase via a direct Redwood contract without long outages.

Specific asks from NewtonCloud:
- Rev-share: Redwood to accept 60% to NewtonCloud / 40% to Redwood for first 12 months (pilot).
- Payment terms: Net-60 for first invoice (their procurement constraint).
- Fallback: automatic redirect to a direct invoice/contract if AWS private offer is rejected or delayed beyond 30 days.

They understand this is nonstandard — can we get internal approval path and any constraints we need to flag? Attaching a draft MOP and a mutual action plan.

Best,
Ola
NewtonCloud — Head of Partnerships

Attachments: NewtonCloud_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet), NewtonCloud_SOW.pdf (referenced)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private offer for NewtonCloud — request for commission change and fallback

Team — forwarding NewtonCloud's asks. High level: they want a one-time deviation to rev-share (we'd effectively worsen our take for 12 months) + net-60 + an operational fallback if AWS private offer stalls. Marissa, this is your opportunity; can you summarize expected ARR and GTM rationale? Karthik, please list Deal Desk constraints and any marketplace approval precedents. Evelyn + Laura, please flag finance/legal risks (cash timing, indemnities, DocuSign flow) so we can give a decision by EOD Wednesday.

Quick context for approvers: NewtonCloud is in late-stage talks with two strategic customers (pilot commitments totaling ~$240k ARR annualized). The pilot is contingent on marketplace availability in Q4. If we refuse the fallback they prefer, NewtonCloud may delay.

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): NewtonCloud_PrivateOffer_Draft_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer for NewtonCloud — request for commission change and fallback

Kim / Team,

Summary from GTM: NewtonCloud is strategic in our ADP pipeline for the east coast retail vertical — quick win and strong reference potential. ARR math: pilot customers ~240k ARR if they convert; expansion potential in their account network could add 600k+ over 18 months. Asking Redwood to accept a 40/60 split (Redwood 40%) for 12 months reduces our marketplace gross margin but materially accelerates listing and conversion.

Proposed commercial compromise to approve (subject to finance/legal guardrails):
- Approve the 40% Redwood / 60% NewtonCloud split for an initial 12-month pilot only, with automatic reversion to standard terms unless both sides agree to extend.
- Approve net-60 for first invoice only; subsequent invoices revert to standard net-30. Finance escrow or milestone-triggered invoicing recommended.
- Fallback policy: If AWS private offer is not active within 30 days of the agreed go-live, allow purchase via a direct Redwood contract for the pilot customers; Redwood will bill at the private-offer price and treat revenue as if listed (to honor NewtonCloud commission share). Any invoicing must include a purchase order number and a signed SOW.

I recommend final approval contingent on: Evelyn signs off on cashflow mitigation plan; Laura signs off on fallback indemnity language and DocuSign routing to ensure marketplace listing isn't used to bypass tax/compliance checks. If approved, Marissa will own communications and the offer activation flow.

—Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer for NewtonCloud — request for commission change and fallback

Team,

Finance perspective: we can support a temporary change to rev-share and payment terms with conditions to protect Redwood cashflow and recognition. Required controls: 
- Milestone-based invoice schedule for the first 90 days (e.g., 50% on signed SOW, 50% on go-live) even if NewtonCloud requests net-60; net-60 ok for balance if milestone payments are observed.
- Escalating credit check: NewtonCloud must provide PO/BG for pilot customers or acceptable credit references.
- Clear accounting treatment: revenue recognized for salesforce compensation will follow standard rules; accounting will treat diverted marketplace revenue consistently.

If legal accepts fallback indemnity, I can sign off on the temporary split. We should build a short playbook so operations know how to record revenue when fallback is used.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer for NewtonCloud — request for commission change and fallback

All,

Legal review — high level notes and required language: 
1) Commission Adjustment: Draft an amendment to the standard marketplace addendum specifying the temporary split (Redwood 40% / NewtonCloud 60%) and an automatic expiration date (12 months) with an explicit reversion clause. Include a clawback provision if NewtonCloud fails to meet pilot conversion milestones.
2) Fallback Mechanism: Accept fallback as a commercial remediation but limit exposure:
   - Fallback only available to named pilot customers in the mutual action plan (no broad entitlement).
   - Customer purchases via direct contract must include the same product SKU and price as the private offer; Redwood will invoice but must include NewtonCloud's PO and reference.
   - Add indemnity language protecting Redwood for any tax/VAT differences or marketplace-specific compliance obligations that NewtonCloud would have covered had the listing gone live.
3) DocuSign & Marketplace Flow: We will need coordinated routing — internal legal + salesops sign-off prior to invoking fallback. Also require an internal approval ticket in Deal Desk and a HubSpot stage change to prevent duplicates.

If the team agrees to the compromise terms above and provides the PO/credit assurance, legal can produce the amendment text by COB Thursday. Approve subject to that amendment and the finance milestones.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

---

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa to confirm expected pilot customers and secure POs (by 2025-09-18).
- Karthik to create Deal Desk approval ticket and update HubSpot deal record (RWI-2025-671).
- Evelyn to prepare milestone invoicing schedule and playbook for ops.
- Laura to draft marketplace amendment and fallback clause for DocuSign routing.

Attachments: NewtonCloud_PrivateOffer_Draft_v2.pdf, NewtonCloud_MutualActionPlan.xlsx
